arbitration: settling a dispute through a neutral judge
ballistic: fired on a high curved path
blockade: stopping goods or people from entering or leaving
coalition: group of parties or countries working together
counteroffensive: attack made in reply to an enemy attack
deterrence: stopping an attack by showing strength
devaluation: official lowering of a currency's value
diaspora: people living outside their home country
disinvestment: government selling its share in companies
disputed: claimed by more than one side
escalation: making a conflict bigger or more serious
extradition: handing over an accused person to another country
fiscal: related to government finances; 'this fiscal' means this financial year
genocide: deliberate killing of a whole group of people
hegemony: dominance of one power over others
hostage: person held by force to make demands
humanitarian: related to helping people in need
hypersonic: faster than five times the speed of sound
impeachment: formal process to remove a top official
indigenous: made or developed in the country itself
jurisdiction: official power to make legal decisions
liquidity: availability of cash in the system
mediation: help from a third party to settle a dispute
militant: person using violence for a cause
ordinance: temporary law made when Parliament is not sitting
paramilitary: armed force similar to an army
provocation: action meant to anger or start a fight
referendum: public vote on a single question
remittances: money sent home by people working abroad
repatriation: sending people back to their own country
repo: rate at which RBI lends to banks
sanctions: penalties, like trade bans, put on a country
secession: breaking away to form a separate country
sedition: speech or action against the state
sovereignty: full power of a country to govern itself
stimulus: government push to boost the economy
subsidy: money the government pays to lower prices
yield: return earned on an investment or bond
